tools.name: Miro
tools.desc: Collaborative online whiteboarding platform for teams
pros: Ready to use out of the box, no local install or maintenance
Free tier available, try before you upgrade
cons: Advanced features and higher limits usually require a paid plan
Requires internet connection, unusable offline
usage:
Step: Open the official site and sign up
Click the red "Visit official site" button to open the Miro homepage. Find "Sign Up" and log in with email or Google/GitHub.
Tip:
If the site won’t load, check your connection or try another browser.

Step: Pick the plan that fits you
New users usually get a free trial or free quota. Start with the Free tier before upgrading.
Check:
After sign-up you should see the Dashboard home.

Step: Create your first task / project
Click "New" or "Create New" and follow the guide. Pick the first template to start.
Tip:
Don’t start with a complex request. Test with one simple sentence, e.g. "Summarize this page into 3 points".

Step: Review and save the result
When done, the tool shows the result. Export, copy the link, or save locally.
Check:
If unhappy, click "Regenerate" or tweak the prompt and try again.
tools.detail: Miro is a collaborative online whiteboarding platform designed for teams to work together in real-time. It allows users to create, share, and collaborate on visual ideas, diagrams, and presentations. Key features include a vast library of templates, integrations with popular tools like Slack and Microsoft Teams, and the ability to import and export files in various formats. Miro is ideal for teams of all sizes and industries, from startups to large enterprises. It is particularly useful for brainstorming sessions, project planning, and design collaboration. Pros include its intuitive interface, robust collaboration features, and extensive library of resources. Limitations may include a learning curve for new users and the need for a stable internet connection.
